properties.name: A served item is removed only after a release that announced it: the registry, the mark, the notice, the tool stub, and a surface check that shrinks only through a deprecating release
properties.rationale:
WHY: Anthony amended the requirement on 2026-10-13 rather than retire it (judgement pass, "Go with your recommendations"). In the requirement's words: "never removed" becomes "never removed WITHOUT A RELEASE OF NOTICE"; anything a client can call or read (a tool, a field, a node type, a reply shape) is retired in two releases, "(1) A DEPRECATING release, in which it still works, says it is going (in its tool description, or in describe_schema for a schema item), and the changelog carries a 'What to do' line ... (2) The NEXT release removes it"; and "The check that the served surface only grows becomes a check that it shrinks only through a deprecating release." dec:anchor-retire-or-implement (retire the unused Anchor type) waits on this rule and is the next PR; this one checked that the registry, the describe_schema mark, the notice and the vocabulary record all cover a node type.

THE TOOL RULE, reconciled rather than overridden: dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first says a removal "ships first as a stub under the old name that refuses and names the replacement — for one release". The amendment calls itself "the same discipline the accepted tool rule already applies to tools", but the two are not identical: the tool rule's stub REFUSES, while the amendment's deprecating release still WORKS. They compose without conflict as three stages for a tool: deprecate (works, marked), then remove (the registry entry stays one more release, and the old name is refused with what to do, in a session and at the --call door), then the entry comes out. The surface check asserts that stub: a deprecated tool that is no longer listed must still answer its old name with the release's what-to-do. The tool rule's other condition, usage evidence from more than one project, belongs to the retiring decision named in each entry; no code can check it.

WHY THE NOTICE IS A REPLY FIELD: an added field is what the surface rule always allowed, and it reaches both client populations. A structured reader reads it in structuredContent, and a content-only client (Alex's Grok) reads it in the text block content_policy builds from the structured reply. _meta would never reach a model. Who tells Alex, and how, is Anthony's open decision (D3); the release-cut step says the telling is owed before a release ships and does not choose.

TESTS FIRST (513f60e3d): on main they do not build, because the registry does not exist. With an inert registry, 11 of 15 failed on the missing behaviour, and the 4 before-and-after invariants passed. All pass at afb1e1aed. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Builds the retirement rule of req:the-mcp-server-keeps-working-as-is-and-door-improvements-are-additive-or-opt-in (amended 2026-10-13) and deprecates nothing. NEW: deprecation::REGISTRY (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/deprecation.rs, art:deprecation), empty, the one place a deprecation is declared (item, deprecated_in, what_to_do, decision). CHANGED: service.rs (art:service) marks tools/list through the one served list, adds `deprecation_notice` to a call that uses a deprecated item, and refuses a removed tool's old name with what to do; tools/query.rs (art:tools-query) marks describe_schema and lists `deprecations` in its full answer; main.rs (art:main) gives the --call door the same stub refusal; AGENTS.md (art:agent-instructions) states the rule, the two releases, the tool's extra step and the release-cut step; changelog.d/README.md (art:changelog-fragments-readme) gives the Deprecated-entry convention. THE CHECK: tests/the_mcp_surface_only_grows.rs (art:the-mcp-surface-only-grows-test, registered now) records each release's vocabulary and deprecations at a bless and passes a removal only when the record marks it deprecated; its record is re-blessed from the published v0.84.0 binary (tools and replies byte-identical, deprecations [], vocabulary added). NEW TESTS: art:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it-test and art:every-deprecation-is-announced-in-the-changelog-test, implementing ver:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it (passing). DESIGN: cap:a-served-item-is-removed-only-after-a-release-that-announced-it (realized) and the release-cut step cap:a-cuts-release-notes-say-what-is-going-and-what-has-gone (planned, flow:release-cut step 2), both SATISFIES the requirement; the first GOVERNED_BY dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first. With the registry empty nothing a client sees changes: all 197 toolsnaps match.
